entry.title: What would a wormhole look like in the real life?
entry.summary: I wrote my own wormhole renderer to visualize wormholes in 3D environments (forest + mars) and explained how it works. Prepare your mind to comprehend 4D geometry.

entry.title: Spherical portals explain dark energy?
entry.summary: What happens if a portal is shaped like a sphere? Spoiler: nothing... until you put one inside the other. Then space repeats infinitely, physics gets weird, and gravity starts acting like dark energy.

entry.title: Portals can simulate a Klein bottle, so I calculated gravity on it
entry.summary: Continuing to explore how portals affect gravity - this time looking at closed spaces (torus, Klein bottle, etc.) and pocket dimension (partially closed). In the process, I discovered an unexpected phenomenon called self-force, which makes me genuinely afraid of a portal into…

entry.title: Portals must bend gravity, actually
entry.summary: Portals don't conserve energy? Actually, no. We just need to allow gravity to flow through portals. And once we do that, portals start to conserve energy and make sense physically. But how can we do that? How does this change the portal's behavior? And how does this affect…

entry.title: Antiportal - what is it and how does it explain pocket dimension?
entry.summary: In the previous video, we learned how to create pocket dimension when one portal is smaller than the other. But is it possible when both portals are the same size? In this video, we will explore this problem from all sides and create a powerful approach for simulating portal…

entry.title: Why do portals create pocket dimension when you put a small portal into a bigger portal?
entry.summary: What will happen if you take two portals, shrink one of them and place it inside the other? Finally, this solution has been found, and according to it, a pocket dimension should be created! And at the end, we discuss portal physics, because there has been a paradigm shift…

entry.title: Portals with an impossible shape (cylinder, Mobius strip, knot)

entry.title: Portal with 3 parts: is this possible?

entry.title: What happens if you put a portal in a portal? Simulation and explanation
entry.summary: This video shows the solution to the most complex portal riddle: "What will happen if we put one portal into another?". I explained how this works and how I programmed this.

entry.title: fopply — my program for step-by-step algebraic calculations
entry.summary: This program lets you do algebraic calculations step by step and stay in control of them. It works by smartly applying formulas to the original expression. Here is the devlog of the program together with a description of the idea behind it.

entry.title: Moving my blog to Zola and why it's better than Jekyll
entry.summary: Zola is a great static site generator. I moved my blog to it, and it inspired me to implement many cool features and to speed up the blog. This article focuses on the pros and cons of Zola as a static site generator.

entry.title: Speeding up a static website
entry.summary: My blog used to load slowly and lag a lot, even though it was a static site. Here is how I got maximum loading speed, minimal traffic and a score of 100 in Lighthouse.

entry.title: New features of this blog

And how do you describe that the probability increases given some event? I propose an interesting idea of "confidences", which are meant to solve this.
